claims.entity: Bonneville Power Administration (asset-controlling supplier system emission factor, regulator-assigned)
claims.metric: System emission factor for BPA specified-source wholesale power, data year 2027
claims.unit: metric tons CO2e per MWh (source: 'MT CO2e per MWh')
claims.boundary: Assigned by Washington Ecology from BPA's verified calendar year 2025 reported data, for transactions of BPA specified-source power delivered in 2027. A regulatory accounting factor for power sold into Washington (and, at the same value, California), not an inventory of BPA plant emissions, not a marginal factor, and not the Northwest grid average. The Ecology page prints it as a BPA-specific factor but the numbers are regulator-assigned, not published by BPA.

source.title: Asset-Controlling Supplier (ACS) Systems Emission Factor (Pub. No. 25-14-079)

claims.quote: Table 1: Asset-Controlling Supplier (ACS) System Emission Factor (EF) for data year 2027 (reported in 2028) ... Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) 0.0493 MT CO2e per MWh
claims.derived: 0.0493 metric tons per MWh x 1,000 kg per ton = 49.3 kg CO2e/MWh = 49.3 g CO2e/kWh. 2027 / 2024 = 0.0493 / 0.0160 = 3.1x. 2027 against the mean of CARB's 13 BPA values for 2013 to 2025 (0.0198): 2.5x.
claims.limit: A regulator-assigned system factor from a hydro-heavy supplier; it is neither the publisher's own inventory nor comparable to eGRID, AVERT, or Cambium without naming the method.

The source prints 'megatons' per MWh, which cannot be right for a factor of 0.02; the abbreviation MT and the CARB check show metric tons. The average is also stale for current use: data years 2025 to 2027 are about 0.045 to 0.050 (dem-099).
